full_judgment:
"6. Amendment of section 6, Act XL of 1958—In the said Act, in section 6,— 

 This amendment it appears made the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure applicable in the Special cases triable by the Special Judges, in so far as they are not inconsistent with the said Act of 1958 (Act No. XL of 1958). It also appears in Section 8 of the aforesaid Ordinance as follows — 

 9. This is special provision made for quick disposal of the cases which were revived under the aforesaid Ordinance. The Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 is a special statute and section 6 as quoted above provides that the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (V of 1898), shall, in so far as they are not inconsistent with this Act, apply to the proceedings of the Court of a Special Judge and for the purpose of the said provisions, the Court of Special Judge shall be deemed to be a Court of Session trying cases without jury or assessors. For conclusion of a trial by the Special Judge there is no specified time limit; nevertheless, provisions for time limit under section 339C of the Code are applicable to a trial by a Special Judge. The provisions of section 8 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act is intended for "more speedy trial" of certain offences. Section 339C of the Code is intended for expeditious disposal of criminal cases. The Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 provides that provisions of the Code shall apply if they are not inconsistent with its own provisions. Here in this case it appears from the perusal of the record that earlier the proceeding was stopped under section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure as the trial Court failed to conclude the trial within the statutory period. Thereafter, on the promulgation of Ordinance No. III of 1987 the case was revived. Now the question arises whether after the revival of the case, the provision of section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure will be applicable, or the provision of section 8 of the aforesaid Ordinance will be applicable. Section 6 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 provides that the provisions of the Code shall applicable in the proceedings of the Court of a Special Judge in so far as they are not inconsistent with the Criminal Law Amendment Act and I have already found that section 339C of the Code has been included in the statute for speedy disposal of the Criminal Cases. Section 339C(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure provides that a Sessions Judge, an Additional Sessions Judge or an Assistant Sessions Judge which according to section 6 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act shall be deemed to be Special Judges shall conclude the trial of the case within 240 days, the date on which the case is received for trial and sub-section (6) of Section 339C of the Code provides that in determining the time for the purpose of a trial only the working days of the Court shall be counted and it has been held by our Appellate Division in the case of Abul Kashem and another Vs. State, reported in 40 DLR (AD) 97 that "Working days" shall be understood to mean the "Working days" during which the learned Judge will hold the charge of the trial Court and in the reported decision, it appears that the trial Court was in-Charge of the District and Sessions Judge for 53 days and those 53 days were not counted in computing the specified time for the conclusion of trial and relying on this decision the learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that the present incumbent Special Judge joined that station on 12.12.88 and from that date if the calculation is made the trial Court had another 221 days for the disposal of the present case. 

 10. But it has been decided by our Appellate Division in the case of Kamruzzaman Vs. State, reported in 42 DLR (AD) 219 that the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure will be made applicable under section 6 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 if the same is not inconsistent with the provision of that Act. Here in this case, it appears that by Ordinance No. III of 1987 the provisions of the Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958 has been further amended and section 8 of this Ordinance provides that cases revived under this Ordinance shall have to be concluded within two years from the date of commencement of this Ordinance. If the provisions of section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure is made applicable in the present case, it will be inconsistent with the provision of this Ordinance as under section 339C only the working days of the Judge concerned is to be calculated, whereas this Ordinance, which amended the Criminal Law Amendment Act which is special law, has made it incumbent on the trial Court to conclude the trial within two years from the date of commencement of the Ordinance. The Act provides that provisions of the Code shall apply to a case under the Act if they are not inconsistent with its own provisions and the Code of Criminal Procedure provides that its provisions shall not affect any special law unless specifically provided otherwise. Section 1(2) of the Code says that in the absence of any specific provision to the contrary, nothing shall affect any special law now in force. Section 339C of the Code was incorporated in the statute for speedy disposal of the cases and so is the provision of section 8 of the aforesaid Ordinance. But there are certain inconsistencies. If after the revival of the case under the said Ordinance which was earlier stopped under section 339C of the Code the provision of section 339C is made applicable again this will delay the disposal of the cases as under section 339D of the Code only the working days of the concerned Judge shall have to be taken into consideration and in case of the transfer of a Special Judge the time limit of the succeeding Judge shall start from the date of his joining that station which will naturally defeat the provision of section 8 of the aforesaid Ordinance and on that ground I am of the view that section 339C and section 339D(b) of the Code is very much inconsistent with the provision of section 8 of the aforesaid Ordinance and as section 339C and section 339D(b) are inconsistent with the provisions of the aforesaid Ordinance these two sections are not applicable in the cases which were revived under the aforesaid Ordinance.
